headlines.text: It was 2022 when the AEW World Heavyweight Title had a new owner by the end of the night as Jon Moxley vs. Bryan Danielson battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 8.05 ? a real highlight of the night. Moxley put Danielson to sleep with a rear choke on the stage to become a three-time AEW World Champion, capping the tournament that followed the vacating of the title weeks earlier.

That Wednesday in 2022, a new champion was crowned for the ROH World Heavyweight Title as Chris Jericho vs. Claudio Castagnoli battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.86 ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. Jericho snuck in a low blow the referee missed, then finished Castagnoli with the Judas Effect to win the ROH World Title ? his eighth world championship overall.

On this day in 2022, there was a changing of the guard for the AEW World Tag Team Titles as The Acclaimed vs. Swerve in our Glory battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.26 ? a well-paced, entertaining battle ? ending the champion's reign at 4 defenses. The Acclaimed avenged their All Out loss, with Max Caster hitting the Mic Drop on Swerve Strickland to dethrone Swerve In Our Glory and capture their first AEW World Tag Team Championship.

secondaries.text: Back on this day in 2022, PAC vs. Orange Cassidy put the AEW All-Atlantic Title on the line, appearing on Dynamite, rated 6.41.

Looking back to 2022, when Toni Storm vs. Athena vs. Britt Baker vs. Serena Deeb fought tooth and nail for the AEW Women's World Title, appearing on Dynamite, rated 5.83. Athena was challenging for gold for the very first time.
